description: Updates a run's status, and optionally its finished_at timestamp and error_message.
signature: def update_run_status(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, status: str, *, finished_at: str | None = None, error_message: str | None = None) -> None
docstring:
Transition a run to a new status.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    run_id: The run to update.
    status: One of 'pending', 'running', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled'.
    finished_at: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp string; typically provided when status is a terminal state ('succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled').
    error_message: Populated when status='failed'.

Returns:
    None.

Raises:
    StorageError: If run_id does not exist, or status is not one of the five allowed values.
postconditions: get_run(conn, run_id).status == status after a successful call
If finished_at is provided, get_run(conn, run_id).finished_at reflects it exactly

edge_cases.expected_behavior: StorageError, not a silent no-op (distinct from delete_run's no-op-on-unknown-id contract, since a status update on a nonexistent run indicates a caller bug)
StorageError before any UPDATE is issued

edge_cases.input: Updating a run that is already in a terminal state to another terminal state (e.g. succeeded -> failed)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: allowed at the storage layer; storage enforces no state-machine transition rules, only the CHECK-constrained value set -- orchestration is responsible for not doing this

unit_tests.name: test_update_to_running_then_succeeded
unit_tests.description: Two sequential updates land correctly and finished_at is set on the second.
unit_tests.expected: get_run reflects status='succeeded' and the given finished_at

unit_tests.name: test_unknown_run_id_raises
unit_tests.description: Updating a nonexistent run_id raises StorageError.
